answers.explanation: One small event: an interrupt is exactly right. DMA is for big, fast transfers.
Per-byte interrupts would leave the CPU no time for anything else.
Registers are the fastest storage there is, and the compiler puts hot variables there.
Tape is the cheapest per byte, and slowness doesn't matter for an archive.
It's a trap: a software-generated interrupt.
The bootstrap program initializes the system and loads the kernel.
Each device has an entry with its type, address, and state.
The cache is checked first; on a miss the hardware fills it from memory.
